Behaviour and state: no way to say that one element changes another.

What the render gate refuses (blockedNodes.ts and renderVocabulary.ts): embedded content (iframe, object, embed, ...), although these are ordinary content elements, and attributes that act by themselves (ping, the shadow root ones).
Media queries beyond width: print, dark mode and reduced motion have no home.
CSS that applies to the document rather than a node (`:root`, view transitions, `@page`, `@layer`): the route owns `html`, so these close with the page-level items of the plan.
An HTML attribute whose name is also a CSS property (width, height) is read as a style, so the editor loses the attribute: a canvas bitmap size or an image size hint is not the same as a declaration.

At-rules: no way to store @keyframes, @container, @supports, @font-face and the rest.
JSX that is a program, not markup: reported as left over by the static import, as the plan requires.
